headline: PM Modi Highlights Youth-Led Momentum of Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan
fullText:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

PM Modi Highlights Youth-Led Momentum of Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan

PM appreciates ‘Nasha-Mukti Ka Sandesh’ and youth-led creative communication

27 SEP 2026 4:54PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today highlighted the growing participation of young people across the country in the Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan, during the 138th episode of his monthly radio programme Mann Ki Baat. He noted that millions of young people have taken a resolve to stay away from drugs and substance abuse and are also taking responsibility for spreading awareness among others.

The Prime Minister said that the 100-week Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Abhiyan brings together volunteers associated with Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) and the National Service Scheme (NSS), along with schools, colleges, universities and various social and spiritual organisations. He noted that thousands of pledge ceremonies and awareness programmes have been organised across the country in recent days as part of the campaign.

Highlighting the importance of youth-led communication, the Prime Minister particularly appreciated the ‘Nasha-Mukti Ka Sandesh’ initiative. He observed that young people are taking the message against substance abuse to communities in their own languages and through their own creative forms of expression.

Recalling his earlier appeal to young people through Mann Ki Baat to contribute their creativity to the campaign, the Prime Minister expressed appreciation for the response from youth across the country. Various competitions, including anthem, slogan-writing and street-play competitions, have been organised through the MY Bharat platform to encourage young people to use their creativity in spreading awareness.

The Prime Minister also highlighted the growing use of social media by youth to amplify the campaign message through creative content using the hashtag #NashaMuktYuva. He noted that in the campaign, the message, medium and driving energy are being led by the youth themselves.

As part of the campaign's continued outreach, activities such as health check-ups and meditation camps will also be organised in the coming days to promote healthy lifestyles and holistic well-being among young people.

The Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Abhiyan is being implemented as a sustained 100-week campaign to strengthen awareness among young people, encourage community participation and promote a collective resolve against substance abuse. Through MY Bharat, NSS, educational institutions and partner organisations, the campaign seeks to harness the energy and creativity of India's youth towards building a healthier and drug-free generation.

Pawan Singh Faujdar

headline: EXERCISE TARANG SHAKTI 2026: “POWER IN PARTNERSHIP”
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

EXERCISE TARANG SHAKTI 2026: “POWER IN PARTNERSHIP”

IAF COMMENCES OPERATIONAL PHASE AT JODHPUR

27 SEP 2026 4:45PM by PIB Delhi

Following the inaugural ceremony held yesterday, the Indian Air Force (IAF) is set to commence the operational phase of Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 at Air Force Station Jodhpur. Being conducted from 26 September to 12 October 2026, the multilateral air exercise is themed “Power in Partnership”, underscoring the strength that comes from working together, sharing expertise and building interoperability among partner air forces.

Seven Friendly Foreign Countries (FFCs) — Australia, the United States of America, the United Arab Emirates, France, Germany, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh — are participating in the exercise. The foreign aircraft taking part include the F-35 Lightning II, Rafale, F-16, A400M, MRTT, C-130, C-130J and KC-30A, bringing together a diverse mix of combat, airlift and air-to-air refuelling capabilities.

Building on the successful inaugural edition in 2024, Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 provides participating air forces an opportunity for advanced joint training, exchange of operational expertise and consolidation of professional experience. The participating contingents will operate alongside the IAF, employing frontline combat platforms and support elements across a range of missions. Several other FFCs will also participate as observers.

The exercise will facilitate professional interaction among aircrew, mission planners and operational support personnel, with emphasis on interoperability, mutual learning, aerospace safety and enhanced understanding of operational procedures. The interaction will provide participating forces an opportunity to operate together, share experiences and gain a better understanding of each other's capabilities and operating philosophies.

This edition of Tarang Shakti has a wider canvas beyond flying operations, with a range of professional, cultural and outreach activities planned during the exercise. These include a dedicated seminar, industrial tour for the participating foreign contingents, Sekhon Marathon, heritage tours and yoga sessions. These engagements will provide opportunities for professional exchange, exposure to India's aerospace and industrial ecosystem, and greater interaction and camaraderie among the participating contingents.

Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 provides the IAF an opportunity to demonstrate its operational capabilities, professional standards and institutional ethos, while highlighting India's growing indigenous aerospace and defence capabilities. The exercise, under the theme “Power in Partnership”, reinforces the importance of cooperation, interoperability and mutual trust in building enduring partnerships among participating air forces.

The exercise reaffirms India's commitment to constructive defence engagement and enhanced military cooperation in support of regional peace, security and stability, while strengthening partnerships and fostering greater strategic cooperation through shared operational experience.

headline: Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh to Launch Livestock Insurance Portal in New Delhi on 28 September 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh to Launch Livestock Insurance Portal in New Delhi on 28 September 2026

Livestock Insurance Portal to Offer Digital Insurance Services in 11 Regional Languages Along with Hindi and English

27 SEP 2026 3:17PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying (DAHD), Government of India, will launch the Livestock Insurance Portal on 28th September, 2026 in New Delhi, marking an important milestone in the digital transformation of livestock insurance services in the country.

The Portal will be launched by Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj, Government of India.

The Portal will provide a single, integrated digital platform for livestock insurance, enabling streamlined policy issuance, claim processing, monitoring and reporting, in case of animals insured under the Livestock Insurance Scheme of the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying. To promote wider accessibility and ease of use, the Portal will also be available in 11 regional languages apart from Hindi and English, enabling livestock farmers to access information and services in languages familiar to them.

The initiative is aimed at making livestock insurance services more transparent, efficient, accessible and technology-driven, while strengthening risk protection for livestock farmers and supporting the sustainability of their livelihoods.

The Portal will also facilitate better coordination, real-time monitoring and data-driven management of livestock insurance programmes, contributing to improved service delivery across the country.

The launch represents a significant step towards simplifying livestock insurance processes, strengthening institutional efficiency and bringing inclusive, technology-enabled services closer to livestock farmers.

headline: Rajasthan’s Art, Faith, Royalty and Sporting Legacy on Display at PM Mementos e-Auction 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Culture

Rajasthan’s Art, Faith, Royalty and Sporting Legacy on Display at PM Mementos e-Auction 2026

The collection brings together folk deities, traditional art, textiles, heritage sites and sporting memorabilia, offering a glimpse into Rajasthan’s diverse traditions

27 SEP 2026 3:03PM by PIB Delhi

Rajasthan’s rich tapestry of art, devotion, craftsmanship and tradition comes alive in a diverse collection of mementos featured in the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026. The collection brings together 37 artefacts representing the state’s folk deities, traditional paintings, textiles, architectural heritage and sporting achievements.

Among the prominent pieces is a handcrafted Ambabari elephant with Howdah, carved from wood and decorated with traditional patterns. Another handcrafted wooden elephant procession set depicts a royal howdah accompanied by ceremonial attendants.

The collection highlights a silver memento of Veer Tejaji Maharaj depicts the revered folk deity mounted on a horse, while another silver-plated statue portrays him riding his horse with his characteristic spear and snake motif.

The collection includes Pichwai paintings of Shrinathji from Nathdwara, a Phad painting depicting Lakshmi and Narayan and a Pattachitra-style artwork portraying Krishna Raas Leela. These works showcase different forms of devotional storytelling and artistic expression represented in the catalogue.

The cultural diversity of the collection extends to Ajmer Sharif Dargah, represented through both a hand-painted artwork and a framed depiction of the shrine. The catalogue describes the painting as capturing the architectural character of the Dargah and its tradition of welcoming devotees from different faiths.

A decorated turban featuring a stone and feather brooch, a yellow pagdi with multicoloured motifs, and several angavastras featuring gota borders showcase the region’s textile and ornamental traditions.

The collection further features representations of several revered sites and deities, including Kaila Mata of Karauli, Sundha Mata, Khema Baba of Baytu, Brahma Temple in Pushkar and Shri Kalyan Raiji Maharaj. A painting of Mangarh Dham in Banswara also forms part of the collection.

Alongside these cultural and sporting artefacts are historical and contemporary memorabilia, including framed newspaper editions related to the Ayodhya Ram Mandir Pran Pratishtha and a decorative plate artwork issued by BJP Rajasthan.

Together, the 37 mementos present a varied portrait of Rajasthan through its folk traditions, devotional art, painting, textiles, historical heritage, architecture and contemporary achievements, bringing several facets of the state’s cultural identity into the PM Mementos e-Auction.

The 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026, live until 2 October 2026, brings together mementos representing Rajasthan’s rich cultural heritage and traditions. For auction dates, participation details and the complete catalogue, visit the official PM Mementos e-Auction portal: pmmementos.gov.in

headline: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Highlights Uttar Pradesh’s Growing Global Trade and Investment Opportunities
fullText:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Highlights Uttar Pradesh’s Growing Global Trade and Investment Opportunities

UP’s Entrepreneurs to Benefit from Expanding Global Market Access through Free Trade Agreements: Shri Goyal

Uttar Pradesh Targets Increase in Annual Exports from Around ₹2 Lakh Crore to ₹5 Lakh Crore by 2030: Shri Goyal

27 SEP 2026 2:10PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal highlighted that as global markets open up to India through Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), Uttar Pradesh’s entrepreneurs will have greater opportunities to access international markets. Addressing the UP International Trade Show in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, Shri Goyal said that expanding exports, investments and global market access would contribute to the state’s goal of becoming a $1 trillion economy.

Shri Goyal said new investments are expected to flow into India from across the globe and noted that Uttar Pradesh has emerged as a preferred investment destination, supported by favourable industrial policies and proactive industrial schemes. He said major corporations and global investors are arriving across sectors, creating new employment opportunities.

The Minister highlighted the role of modern technology, international enterprises and the evolving craftsmanship and technical skills of Uttar Pradesh’s youth in driving the state’s development. He said international events of this scale provide opportunities for direct access to global markets, enabling Uttar Pradesh’s diverse products, cuisines and services to reach international markets.

Shri Goyal highlighted the international participation at the UP International Trade Show, including six partner countries, hundreds of delegates and exhibitors, and buyer-seller meetings. He noted the participation of international stakeholders and the opportunities created for businesses through the event.

The Minister highlighted the development of expressways, modern airports and industrial parks in Uttar Pradesh and noted the state’s growing presence across sectors including defence, semiconductors, electronics and other modern high-technology domains. He also referred to the expansion of a large robotics manufacturing facility in Greater Noida as an example of modern industrial growth and technological development.

Shri Goyal said the next frontier for Uttar Pradesh’s development lies in expanding exports in global markets, attracting international investments, strengthening tourism and building global recognition for brands from the state. He said Uttar Pradesh is strengthening its foundation for greater global trade and progressing towards its development objectives.

The Minister noted that Uttar Pradesh currently has an annual export volume of around ₹2 lakh crore and has set a target to increase this to ₹5 lakh crore by 2030.

Shri Goyal said the expanding global market access through FTAs, investments, tourism and international recognition of Uttar Pradesh’s products and brands would create new opportunities for the state’s entrepreneurs. He called for active participation and cooperation from the state’s trade and industrial community in taking forward this development journey.

The Minister also highlighted the importance of coordination between the central and state Governments, along with the participation of citizens, youth and stakeholders from the trade and industrial sector, in supporting Uttar Pradesh’s continued economic and export growth.

headline: India Does Not Seek to Occupy Any Country’s Territory, But Will Safeguard Its Security and Strategic Autonomy When Threatened: Rajnath Singh
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

India Does Not Seek to Occupy Any Country’s Territory, But Will Safeguard Its Security and Strategic Autonomy When Threatened: Rajnath Singh

As a Civilizational Power, India’s Rise is in the Interest of the Entire World

India Moving from Defence Importer to Trusted Global Defence Supplier

National Unity is Essential for National Security: Rajnath Singh

27 SEP 2026 1:40PM by PIB Delhi

“India believes in peace and does not seek to occupy the territory of any country. However, peace should not be mistaken for weakness. We seek global stability, but not at the cost of our strategic autonomy. We are firmly committed to safeguarding our security and strategic autonomy when threatened,” said Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh while addressing a Defence Conclave in New Delhi on September 27, 2026.

Raksha Mantri underlined that there can be no scope for dialogue with any country that promotes terrorism against India. “Countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy or provide shelter and support to terrorists must be firmly reminded that terrorism cannot be a strategic asset for any nation. He asserted that as long as a neighbouring country continues to pursue a policy of supporting terrorism, India remains fully entitled to take all necessary measures against terrorism”, he said, referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s remarks at the recent SCO meeting.

Emphasising national unity as a key pillar of national security, the Raksha Mantri stated that the security of the country is not solely the responsibility of the armed forces but a collective responsibility of every citizen. He urged citizens to rise above divisions based on religion, caste, creed, language, region and other identities, and to place national interest above personal and narrow interests.

Shri Rajnath Singh described India as a civilizational power whose rise is based on inclusive development rather than confrontation or disruption. He outlined three foundations of India’s approach: its long democratic and civilizational traditions, the principle of ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’ and the vision of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’, and five strategic pillars—respect, dialogue, prosperity, security and culture.

Focusing on the Global South, Raksha Mantri highlighted India’s growing role as a trusted partner and ‘Vishwa Bandhu’. He noted that under Vaccine Maitri, India supplied more than 30 crore COVID-19 vaccine doses to over 100 countries and has supported developing nations through medicines, digital payment solutions, expertise and resources. He also highlighted initiatives such as the Voice of Global South Summits to advance the interests of developing countries. Emphasising responsible use of power, he called for cooperation even amid competition and inclusive participation in global development.

Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted India’s significant progress towards self-reliance in defence, noting that the country is developing indigenous capabilities ranging from aircraft and drone engines to fifth- and sixth-generation fighter jets. India’s defence exports have grown from just ₹686 crore in 2013–14 to a record ₹38,424 crore in 2025–26, reaching more than 100 countries. After achieving the ₹30,000-crore export target last year, India has now set a target of ₹50,000 crore by 2029.

He emphasised that growing international demand for Indian missiles, radars, ammunition and defence platforms reflects global confidence in India’s technology, quality and delivery capabilities. Consequently, “Made in India” is increasingly emerging not merely as a manufacturing label, but as a symbol of trust in Indian defence capabilities.

Raksha Mantri highlighted the significant increase in defence allocation, which has reached ₹7.85 lakh crore in 2026-27, compared to around ₹2.53 lakh crore in 2013-14. He noted that around 75% of the capital acquisition budget, amounting to ₹1.39 lakh crore, has been earmarked for procurement from the domestic defence industry, thereby strengthening indigenous manufacturing and associated MSME supply chains.

Shri Rajnath Singh stated that the nature of warfare is rapidly changing, with modern conflicts extending beyond conventional domains to cyber, space, electronic and information warfare, alongside emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, drones, autonomous systems, quantum technology and hypersonic systems. He underlined the need for India to develop future-ready capabilities across these domains.

Highlighting India’s efforts to address strategic vulnerabilities in areas such as technology, energy, data and supply chains, the Raksha Mantri said that initiatives are underway to strengthen domestic capabilities in semiconductors and critical minerals, diversify energy sources and enhance energy security.

Emphasising the importance of self-reliance, the Raksha Mantri stated that 509 defence equipment, weapon systems and platforms have been included in five positive indigenisation lists issued by the Armed Forces. DPSUs have also released six indigenisation lists covering 5,417 items, including strategically important LRUs, subsystems, spares and components, of which around 3,300 have been indigenised.

He highlighted the growing participation of the private sector, startups and MSMEs in defence manufacturing. India’s defence ecosystem now includes DPSUs, private industries, more than 16,000 MSMEs, startups, universities and research institutions, with defence manufacturing capabilities emerging across several regions of the country. Investment proposals of about ₹70,000 crore have been received in the Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu Defence Industrial Corridors, with around ₹10,000 crore already invested.

Raksha Mantri also highlighted the role of the SRIJAN and SRIJAN DEEP portals in strengthening indigenous defence supply chains. He stated that around 33,000 imported items have been identified for import substitution through SRIJAN, of which approximately 15,700 have been indigenised. SRIJAN DEEP has created a national digital database covering more than 40,000 manufacturers and sellers and lakhs of products.

Shri Rajnath Singh underlined the transformation of the DPSU and Ordnance Factory ecosystem, noting that corporatisation of the Ordnance Factories has enhanced their technology orientation, output and accountability. He stated that all 16 DPSUs are currently operating without losses and are increasing their focus on research, development and exports.

Highlighting the role of youth and innovation, he said that iDEX and iDEX-Prime are providing opportunities for startups and innovators to contribute to national security, while programmes such as ADITI are supporting advanced defence technologies. As of March 2026, 676 startups and innovators had been engaged through iDEX and 551 contracts signed. The Ministry has also approved procurement worth more than ₹2,400 crore from startups/MSMEs and development projects worth over ₹1,500 crore.

A significant announcement was the decision to transfer DRDO-developed technologies for conventional missile systems to eligible Indian industries, enabling qualifying private companies to undertake production. Shri Rajnath Singh said the move would strengthen the preparedness of the Armed Forces and facilitate timely delivery of missiles. He added that DRDO is increasingly being positioned to focus on research and development while industry assumes a greater role in production.

Raksha Mantri concluded that India’s objective is to build indigenous capabilities across the entire defence spectrum—from individual components to complete weapon systems—and to develop technologies domestically rather than remain dependent on imports. He stressed that this approach is aimed at strengthening strategic autonomy, defence preparedness and a resilient indigenous defence-industrial ecosystem.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS

- **Future Technologies**: Emphasis on developing capabilities in AI, drones, cyber warfare, space, and quantum technologies.
- **Global Outreach**: Supplied over 30 crore COVID-19 vaccine doses globally under Vaccine Maitri; active in Voice of Global South Summits.
- **Technology Transfer**: Decision announced to transfer DRDO-developed conventional missile technologies.
- **Civil-Military Integration**: National unity emphasized as crucial for national security; urged citizens to transcend divisions.

### ARTICLE
Ministry of Defence, India Does Not Seek to Occupy Any Country’s Territory, But Will Safeguard Its Security and Strategic Autonomy When Threatened: Rajnath Singh. As a Civilizational Power, India’s Rise is in the Interest of the Entire World. India Moving from Defence Importer to Trusted Global Defence Supplier. National Unity is Essential for National Security: Rajnath Singh. 27 SEP 2026 1:40 PM by PIB Delhi. “India believes in peace and does not seek to occupy the territory of any country. However, peace should not be mistaken for weakness. We seek global stability, but not at the cost of our strategic autonomy. We are firmly committed to safeguarding our security and strategic autonomy when threatened,” said Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh while addressing a Defence Conclave in New Delhi on September 27, 2026. Raksha Mantri underlined that there can be no scope for dialogue with any country that promotes terrorism against India. “Countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy or provide shelter and support to terrorists must be firmly reminded that terrorism cannot be a strategic asset for any nation.” He asserted that as long as a neighbouring country continues to pursue a policy of supporting terrorism, India remains fully entitled to take all necessary measures against terrorism, referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s remarks at the recent SCO meeting. Emphasising national unity as a key pillar of national security, the Raksha Mantri stated that the security of the country is not solely the responsibility of the armed forces but a collective responsibility of every citizen. He urged citizens to rise above divisions based on religion, caste, creed, language, region and other identities, and to place national interest above personal and narrow interests. Shri Rajnath Singh described India as a civilizational power whose rise is based on inclusive development rather than confrontation or disruption. He outlined three foundations of India’s approach: its long democratic and civilizational traditions, the principle of ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’ and the vision of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’, and five strategic pillars—respect, dialogue, prosperity, security and culture. Focusing on the Global South, Raksha Mantri highlighted India’s growing role as a trusted partner and ‘Vishwa Bandhu’. He noted that under Vaccine Maitri, India supplied more than 30 crore COVID-19 vaccine doses to over 100 countries and has supported developing nations through medicines, digital payment solutions, expertise and resources. He also highlighted initiatives such as the Voice of Global South Summits to advance the interests of developing countries. Emphasising responsible use of power, he called for cooperation even amid competition and inclusive participation in global development. Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted India’s significant progress towards self-reliance in defence, noting that the country is developing indigenous capabilities ranging from aircraft and drone engines to fifth- and sixth-generation fighter jets. India’s defence exports have grown from just ₹686 crore in 2013–14 to a record ₹38,424 crore in 2025–26, reaching more than 100 countries. After achieving the ₹30,000-crore export target last year, India has now set a target of ₹50,000 crore by 2029. He emphasised that growing international demand for Indian missiles, radars, ammunition and defence platforms reflects global confidence in India’s technology, quality and delivery capabilities. Consequently, “Made in India” is increasingly emerging not merely as a manufacturing label, but as a symbol of trust in Indian defence capabilities. Raksha Mantri highlighted the significant increase in defence allocation, which has reached ₹7.85 lakh crore in 2026-27, compared to around ₹2.53 lakh crore in 2013-14. He noted that around 75% of the capital acquisition budget, amounting to ₹1.39 lakh crore, has been earmarked for procurement from the domestic defence industry, thereby strengthening indigenous manufacturing and associated MSME supply chains. Shri Rajnath Singh stated that the nature of warfare is rapidly changing, with modern conflicts extending beyond conventional domains to cyber, space, electronic and information warfare, alongside emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, drones, autonomous systems, quantum technology and hypersonic systems. He underlined the need for India to develop future-ready capabilities across these domains. Highlighting India’s efforts to address strategic vulnerabilities in areas such as technology, energy, data and supply chains, the Raksha Mantri said that initiatives are underway to strengthen domestic capabilities in semiconductors and critical minerals, diversify energy sources and enhance energy security. Emphasising the importance of self-reliance, the Raksha Mantri stated that 509 defence equipment, weapon systems and platforms have been included in five positive indigenisation lists issued by the Armed Forces. DPSUs have also released six indigenisation lists covering 5,417 items, including strategically important LRUs, subsystems, spares and components, of which around 3,300 have been indigenised. He highlighted the growing participation of the private sector, startups and MSMEs in defence manufacturing. India’s defence ecosystem now includes DPSUs, private industries, more than 16,000 MSMEs, startups, universities and research institutions, with defence manufacturing capabilities emerging across several regions of the country. Investment proposals of about ₹70,000 crore have been received in the Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu Defence Industrial Corridors, with around ₹10,000 crore already invested. Raksha Mantri also highlighted the role of the SRIJAN and SRIJAN DEEP portals in strengthening indigenous defence supply chains. He stated that around 33,000 imported items have been identified for import substitution through SRIJAN, of which approximately 15,700 have been indigenised. SRIJAN DEEP has created a national digital database covering more than 40,000 manufacturers and sellers and lakhs of products. Shri Rajnath Singh underlined the transformation of the DPSU and Ordnance Factory ecosystem, noting that corporatisation of the Ordnance Factories has enhanced their technology orientation, output and accountability. He stated that all 16 DPSUs are currently operating without losses and are increasing their focus on research, development and exports. Highlighting the role of youth and innovation, he said that iDEX and iDEX-Prime are providing opportunities for startups and innovators to contribute to national security, while programmes such as ADITI are supporting advanced defence technologies. As of March 2026, 676 startups and innovators had been engaged through iDEX and 551 contracts signed. The Ministry has also approved procurement worth more than ₹2,400 crore from startups/MSMEs and development projects worth over ₹1,500 crore. A significant announcement was the decision to transfer DRDO-developed technologies for conventional missile.

fullText:
Ministry of Agriculture &

Two-Day National Conference on Rabi Campaign 2026 to Begin Tomorrow in New Delhi

Conference to Focus on Strengthening Centre–State Coordination and Evolving an Outcome-Oriented Strategy for Agriculture

State Agriculture Ministers, senior officials of the Central and State Governments, ICAR and other stakeholders to deliberate on key priorities and preparedness for the forthcoming Rabi season

27 SEP 2026 10:19AM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, Government of India, will organise the National Conference on Agriculture for Rabi Campaign 2026 on 28–29 September 2026 at the Bharat Ratna C. Subramaniam Auditorium, NASC Complex, Pusa, New Delhi. The Conference will be inaugurated by Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Union Minister of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, and will bring together State Agriculture Ministers, senior officials of the Central and State Governments, ICAR and other stakeholders to deliberate on key priorities and preparedness for the forthcoming Rabi season.

The two-day Conference will focus on strengthening Centre–State coordination and evolving a coordinated, outcome-oriented strategy for enhancing agricultural production, productivity, sustainability and farmers’ incomes. The deliberations will also build upon the key learnings and outcomes of the recently held Zonal Conferences on Agriculture.

The first day will comprise three rounds of parallel thematic group discussions covering three broad areas: Atmanirbharta, Diversification and Production Growth; Sustainability and Climate-Resilient Agriculture; and Digital Agriculture, Infrastructure, Financing and Risk Management. Key issues to be deliberated upon will include the Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses, oilseeds and oil palm, horticulture, cotton, seed availability and reforms in the seed value chain, natural farming, soil health, farm mechanisation, FPO financing and infrastructure, marketing reforms, PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana, Kisan Credit Card coverage, Digital Agriculture, PM Fasal Bima Yojana, plant protection and agricultural statistics.

The thematic discussions are aimed at identifying key implementation challenges, State-specific priorities and actionable strategies for the Rabi season, with particular emphasis on improving convergence among schemes, strengthening delivery mechanisms and ensuring effective outcomes at the field level.

The second day will focus on the key learnings from the Zonal Conferences and outcomes of the thematic discussions held on the first day. The agenda will include the Rabi season weather outlook, fertilizer availability and balanced use of fertilizers, Digital Agriculture Mission, Farmer Registry, Digital Crop Survey and AgriStack, Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses, National Mission on Edible Oils, crop and seed status, varietal adoption, PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana, marketing reforms and preparation of Agriculture Plans through ATMA and KVKs.

The Conference will also provide an opportunity for State Agriculture Ministers to share their views/experiences, state priorities and suggestions for agricultural development and Rabi season preparedness. The inputs from States, along with the outcomes of the thematic deliberations, are expected to contribute towards a coordinated and outcome-oriented strategy for the Rabi Campaign 2026.

The concluding session will focus on summarizing the deliberations and preparing a robust roadmap for enhancing the crop production of Rabi crops and empowering farmers to fulfil the vision of ‘Atmanirbharta & Viksit Bharat’ ensuring food & nutritional security.

‘Mera Swasthya, Mera Garv’ Activities Held at 400+ Locations Under Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Abhiyan

Over 2.5 Lakh Youth and Citizens Participate in Health, Wellness and De-Addiction Awareness Activities

27 SEP 2026 9:08PM by PIB Delhi

The ‘Mera Swasthya, Mera Garv’ activities, organised under the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Abhiyan, were conducted by MY Bharat and its partner organisations at more than 400 locations across the country, witnessing the participation of over 2.5 lakh youth and citizens.

The nationwide initiative focused on promoting physical and mental well-being among young people while strengthening awareness about the harmful effects of substance abuse. The activities provided participants with opportunities to engage in health and wellness interventions and learn about the importance of adopting healthy and positive lifestyle choices.

As part of the campaign, health check-up camps, health expert sessions and meditation sessions were organised at participating locations. The health-focused activities encouraged young people to pay greater attention to their physical well-being, while expert-led sessions provided an opportunity to engage with health professionals and understand the importance of preventive health and informed choices.

Meditation and wellness sessions further complemented the health interventions by encouraging participants to focus on mental well-being and develop positive approaches towards managing everyday challenges.

Several programmes also featured the Nasha Mukt Yuva Pledge, through which participants expressed their commitment to maintaining a healthy and addiction-free lifestyle. The pledge served as a collective expression of youth participation in the broader campaign for a Nasha Mukt society.

The Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Abhiyan seeks to promote sustained youth engagement through awareness, prevention, healthy lifestyles and positive community participation. The ‘Mera Swasthya, Mera Garv’ activities reinforce the campaign’s focus on making health and well-being an integral part of the Nasha Mukt Yuva movement.

Through the active participation of youth, citizens and partner organisations, the initiative continues to strengthen the message that physical well-being, mental wellness and informed choices are important foundations for building a healthier and Nasha Mukt society.

Union Finance Minister will attend the 11th Annual Meeting of the Board of Governors of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) during the visit

Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman will embark on an official visit to Qatar from 27th to 29th September, 2026. The Union Finance Minister is leading the delegation comprising of Ministry of Finance officials.

In the Annual Meeting of AIIB, the Union Finance Minister will attend as the Indian Governor to the AIIB. India is the second largest shareholder of the bank.

As part of the official visit, the Union Finance Minister is expected to call-on the leadership of the Government of Qatar, and also engage with Qatari business leaders and investors.

The AIIB Annual Meeting witnesses participation of delegations from member countries, and other international organisations. As a multilateral development bank, AIIB is focused on developing sustainable infrastructure in Asia and in promoting investments in infrastructure and other productive sectors with the aim to foster sustainable economic development, create wealth and improve infrastructure connectivity.

Young Indian competitors demonstrate international proficiency across advanced technologies, manufacturing, engineering and specialised services

27 SEP 2026 8:24PM by PIB Delhi

Team India secured 10th position at the 48th WorldSkills Competition, Shanghai 2026, winning 6 Silver Medals and 20 Medal for Excellence as the prestigious international skills competition concluded in Shanghai, China. Improving upon its 13th-place finish at WorldSkills Lyon 2024, where India secured four Bronze Medals and 12 Medal for Excellence, the result marks an important milestone for the country’s skilled youth on the global stage.

The six Silver Medals at WorldSkills Shanghai were won by Smriti Nambiar in Bakery; Mohammed Salam in Dental Prosthetics; Kovid Ajay Gangrade in Digital Interactive Media Design; Parth Vohra in Industrial Design Technology; Mehrunissa Begum in Logistics and Freight Forwarding; and Saniya Joshi in Retail Sales. Their achievements span creative, technical and service-sector skills, reflecting the breadth of Indian talent on the global stage.

India also secured 20 Medal for Excellence across technical, industrial, digital, creative and service skills. Smriti Nambiar, Silver Medallist in Bakery, was recognised as Best of Nation for India.

The six-day international event, held from 22–27 September 2026, brought together over 1,400 young competitors from around 70 countries and regions. Representing India was its largest-ever contingent of 70 competitors participating across 63 skills, spanning emerging technologies, advanced manufacturing, engineering, creative industries and specialised services.

Following four days of intense competition from 23–26 September, the winners were recognised at the grand closing ceremony on 27th September in Shanghai. The ceremony celebrated exceptional technical proficiency, innovation, precision and craftsmanship, bringing together competitors, international delegations, experts and industry representatives from across the world.

Congratulating Team India on its performance, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and the Minister of State for Education, Government of India, said: “Team India’s remarkable performance at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, with 6 Silver Medals and 20 Medal for Excellence, marks a significant leap in our global skills journey. Surpassing our previous performance, our young competitors have demonstrated the growing strength and competitiveness of India’s skilled talent. I congratulate every competitor, expert, trainer and industry partner who contributed to this achievement. Beyond the medals, what makes us proud is the confidence, determination and excellence with which our youth represented India on the world stage. Their success reinforces our commitment to building a future-ready skilling ecosystem and giving every young Indian the opportunity to compete with the best in the world.”

India's achievement reflects the dedication of its young competitors, supported by months of rigorous preparation, specialised training, mentorship and international benchmarking. Medal for Excellence are awarded to competitors who demonstrate a high level of professional proficiency against internationally established WorldSkills standards.

Sharing her perspective on the international exposure gained through the competition, Ms. Manisha Sensarma, Official Delegate, WorldSkills India and Senior Economic Adviser, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Government of India, said: “WorldSkills is as much about learning as it is about competing. Shanghai has given our competitors and experts invaluable exposure to evolving global occupational standards, new technologies and international best practices. Our focus now is to translate these learnings into stronger training methodologies, improved assessment standards and deeper industry engagement, so that the benefits of this experience extend well beyond the competition to India's larger skilling ecosystem.”

A significant feature of India's participation this year was its debut in 11 new and emerging skill categories, including Dental Prosthetics, Digital Interactive Media Design, Intelligent Security Technology, Landscape Gardening, Optoelectronic Technology, Retail Sales, Unmanned Aerial Systems, Industrial Mechanics, Software Testing, Heavy Vehicle Technology and Aircraft Maintenance.

India's entry into these specialised categories reflects the changing contours of the country's skilling ecosystem, with greater emphasis on future-oriented occupations, new technologies and industry-driven competencies.

The participation of young women across diverse technical, creative and service-oriented categories was another important highlight. Women competitors represented India in skills ranging from Chemical Laboratory Technology and Logistics and Freight Forwarding to Fashion Technology, Visual Merchandising, Health and Social Care, Hospitality and other specialised occupations, reflecting the widening opportunities for women in vocational education and skill development.

India's participation at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 was coordinated by the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) under the aegis of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), with support from Sector Skill Councils, industry partners, training institutions, technical experts and other stakeholders.

The competition provided valuable international exposure to Indian competitors and experts, offering insights into global occupational standards, emerging technologies and international best practices that can contribute towards strengthening India's training and assessment ecosystem.

As WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 concludes, Team India's performance celebrates not merely the medals won, but also the commitment, resilience and aspirations of 70 young Indians who represented the country on the world's foremost skills platform. The achievements reaffirm the importance of continued investment in quality skill development, industry partnerships and global benchmarking to nurture a skilled, confident and future-ready workforce.

About WorldSkills: WorldSkills is the world's leading international skills competition, bringing together young professionals from participating countries and regions to demonstrate excellence across a wide range of vocational and technical skills. Held every two years, the competition promotes international standards, facilitates knowledge exchange and inspires young people to pursue skilled careers.

headline: Tourism growth must reach beyond popular destinations and create opportunities for local communities: Union Minister of Tourism & Culture Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat
fullText:
Ministry of Tourism

Tourism growth must reach beyond popular destinations and create opportunities for local communities: Union Minister of Tourism & Culture Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat

National Digital Tourism Stack and National Mission for Alternative Destinations—Dekho Apna Desh 2.0 campaign launched by Union Tourism Minister on World Tourism Day 2026

Ministry of Tourism exchanges MoUs with industry partners to strengthen tourism promotion and responsible travel

27 SEP 2026 8:12PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Tourism celebrated World Tourism Day 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, today, in the presence of Union Minister for Tourism and Culture Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Secretary, Ministry of Tourism, Shri Bhuvnesh Kumar, senior officials of the Ministry and the tourism industry representatives.

On this occasion, the Union Minister launched the National Digital Tourism Stack and the National Mission for Alternative Destinations ­— ­­­­Dekho Apna Desh Campaign 2.0. The Ministry also exchanged five Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with industry partners for joint tourism promotion and marketing.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said, “Tourism is no longer just about visiting places; today’s travellers seek authentic experiences—local cuisine, local art, local traditions and meaningful connections that create memories, not merely photographs.” He further stated, “The next phase of India’s tourism journey must ensure that growth reaches beyond popular destinations, creating opportunities for local communities, entrepreneurs, women and youth while making tourism more balanced, inclusive and sustainable.”

Delivering the welcome address, Shri Bhuvnesh Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Tourism, stated, “Artificial Intelligence, digital platforms and data-driven destination management can make tourism more accessible, responsive and personalised. India has considerable experience in Digital Public Infrastructure, and we are now looking at how these capabilities can be brought together for tourism.”

As part of the programme, Dr. Vivek Raghavan, Co-Founder, Sarvam AI, delivered the keynote address on this year’s World Tourism Day theme, “Digital Agenda and Artificial Intelligence to Redesign Tourism.” He stated that AI has the potential to transform every stage of the tourism journey — from discovering destinations and planning a trip to booking, experiencing and sharing it. The opportunity before us is to use technology to make travel more seamless, personalised and accessible, while creating a customized experience for every traveller."

Presentations on the National Digital Tourism Stack and Nationa Mission for Alternative Destinations – a mission for redistribution of tourism demand & promotion of lesser-known destinations ­— ­­­­Dekho Apna Desh Campaign 2.0 were made by Shri Bhuvnesh Kumar and Shri Suman Billa, Additional Secretary and Director General, Ministry of Tourism, respectively, followed by interactions with industry representatives.

The National Digital Tourism Stack, being developed in collaboration with ONDC and the support of International Centre for DPI Innovation and Advancement (ICDIA), aims to make India’s tourism offerings more discoverable, accessible and trustworthy. This shared digital infrastructure will enable tourism providers to make their offerings available across participating platforms, supported by capabilities such as verified identities and supplier credentials, search and discovery, payments, ratings and grievance redressal. Envisaged as a collaborative effort involving the Ministry, States, Union Territories and industry, the programme will be implemented in phases with a pilot planned for January 2027.

To know more, click here.

The National Mission for Alternative Destionations – a mission for redistribution of tourism demand & promotion of lesser-known destinations ­— ­­­­Dekho Apna Desh Campaign 2.0 seeks to distribute tourism demand more widely by promoting tourism-ready, lesser-known destinations as alternatives or complements to destinations experiencing heavy tourist footfall. In collaboration with States and Union Territories, the initiative will identify destinations with a distinct appeal, adequate infrastructure and accommodation, and the capacity to receive additional visitors sustainably. The initial focus will be on hill and mountain destinations, coastal and waterfront destinations, heritage and cultural towns, and regional pilgrimage destinations.

The initiative will bring together States, Union Territories and tourism industry partners to develop bookable itineraries and packages covering accommodation, transport, meals and local experiences, while creating opportunities for artisans, self-help groups, guides and other local stakeholders. Joint promotion will adopt a social media-first approach, supported by digital campaigns and industry participation. Visitor data and feedback will inform destination management and help monitor tourist footfall against assessed carrying capacity.

On the occasion, the Ministry of Tourism also exchanged five Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with Airbnb India Private Limited, FlixBus India Private Limited, Glance Digital Experience Private Limited (InMobi Group), Eicher Group Foundation and MakeMyTrip (India) Limited to strengthen destination promotion, community participation and responsible tourism. The partnerships cover homestay development and host skilling with Airbnb; destination promotion and responsible travel through intercity mobility with FlixBus; digital tourism content and responsible visitor messaging with Glance; community-led, heritage-based sustainable tourism in the Himalayan region with Eicher Group Foundation; and promotion of unexplored villages, authentic local shopping and Ministry-identified travel initiatives with MakeMyTrip. The collaborations under all these five MoUs are non-commercial, non-financial, non-binding and non-exclusive.

The occasion also marked the launch of a social awareness TV Campaign 2026 on Swachhta, featuring the Hon’ble Prime Minister’s call to citizens to keep pilgrimage sites, temples and heritage sites clean and promote collective participation in cleanliness efforts. India Tourism Statistics 2026 was also released during the event. The launches were accompanied by the screening of the campaign TVC and a video on the publication.

headline: National Zoological Park organises 15th Sunday Bird Walk and 4th Butterfly and Dragonfly Walk, to promote Citizen Science and Biodiversity Conservation
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

National Zoological Park organises 15th Sunday Bird Walk and 4th Butterfly and Dragonfly Walk, to promote Citizen Science and Biodiversity Conservation

NZP to celebrate Wildlife Week 2026 from 2nd - 8th October 2026

27 SEP 2026 7:53PM by PIB Delhi

The National Zoological Park (NZP), New Delhi, organised the fourth edition of the ‘Butterfly and Dragonfly Walk @ NZP’, including the second walk held during the Big Butterfly Month, and the fifteenth edition of the ‘Sunday Bird Walk @ NZP’ as part of its ongoing efforts to promote citizen participation in biodiversity monitoring, species documentation and wildlife conservation awareness. The walks were conducted from 6:30 AM to 10:30 AM under the expert guidance of Sh. Rohit Sharma, Bird Expert, and Sh. Ramver, Butterfly and Dragonfly Expert, along with dedicated volunteers.

The programme received an enthusiastic response from bird and butterfly enthusiasts, nature lovers, students, wildlife photographers and citizens interested in biodiversity conservation. A total of 15 participants took part in the walks. The event was attended by the Director, National Zoological Park, zoo officials and resource experts, who guided and interacted with the participants throughout the activity.

During the walks, participants documented 47 bird species, with observations of more than 750 individual birds, along with 8 butterfly species, 10 dragonfly species and 5 damselfly species in the walk area. The observations provided valuable field-level information and encouraged participants to actively contribute to biodiversity documentation. The observations highlighted the rich diversity of butterflies and odonates within the National Zoological Park and reinforced the importance of regular field-based biodiversity documentation.

The experts shared valuable insights into the ecology, behaviour and conservation of birds, butterflies and dragonflies, highlighting their important ecological roles as pollinators, natural pest controllers and indicators of ecosystem health. The programme also provided participants with an opportunity to connect with nature, strengthen their species-identification skills and develop a deeper appreciation of biodiversity and wildlife conservation.

Addressing the participants, Dr. Sanjeet Kumar, Director, National Zoological Park, highlighted that such nature walks provide valuable opportunities to strengthen field-identification skills, improve understanding of food webs, contribute to biodiversity documentation and foster a deeper appreciation of wildlife and biodiversity conservation. The programme concluded with an interactive discussion, a participant feedback session and a group photograph with the experts and zoo officials.

Participation in each Sunday Nature Walk is limited to 20–25 participants to ensure a meaningful and high-quality learning experience. Prior registration is mandatory and is accepted on a first-come, first-served basis. Interested participants may register through the designated Google Form, which remains open from Monday to Friday each week. The registration link is available on the official website of the National Zoological Park, New Delhi, and through the ‘NZP Sathi’ mobile application.

Further, the NZP New Delhi, would be celebrating the Wildlife Week 2026 from 2nd October to 8th October 2026. A wide range of educational, awareness and participatory activities will be organised during the week to promote wildlife conservation and encourage greater public participation.

The activities planned during Wildlife Week include: Tree Walk, Birds Walk, Butterfly and Dragonfly Walk, Spider and Insect Walk, Reptile, Amphibian and Molluscs Walk, Keeper’s Talk and Enclosure Enrichment, Clay Modeling Competition, Wildlife Poster Making Competition, Debate Competition, Essay Writing Competition, Bird Nest Making competition, Bird Feeder Making competition, Leaf Craft competition, Drawing Competition, Treasure hunt Activity, Rangoli Competition, Quiz Competition, Expert Talk, and Online Photography competition, Online Wildlife Poster Making Competition & online Quiz Activity will be conducted from 02.10.2026 to 08.10.2026.

Detailed information regarding the competitions and other programmes will be made available on the official website of the National Zoological Park, New Delhi, and through the NZP Sathi mobile application. On the occasion of Wildlife Week, the National Zoological Park has invited school students from government and private schools across Delhi-NCR to participate in the various offline and online activities and competitions.

No fee will be charged for any Wildlife Week activity, walk or competition. Free entry to the National Zoological Park will be provided to all participants of Wildlife Week activities and competitions, along with their school teachers, accompanying staff and parents, from 2nd October to 8th October 2026. In addition, children up to 12 years of age will be provided free entry to the National Zoological Park during these dates as part of the Wildlife Week celebrations. Through these initiatives, the NZP seeks to strengthen public engagement with nature, promote citizen science and biodiversity documentation, and foster greater awareness and participation in wildlife conservation.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addresses the inaugural ceremony of centenary year celebrations commemorating birth anniversary of former VHP president Ashok Singhal

Life of Ashok Ji was a confluence of all these virtues—sacrifice, simplicity, exemplary patriotism, devotion to Dharma, and struggle, it’s a matter of pride for all of us to be gathered here on the occasion of his birth centenary

Ashok Ji remained exemplary at every stage of his life, from being a student, volunteer and Pracharak to serving as the International President of VHP, he dedicated his entire life to Hindutva and remained committed to it until his last breath

Despite being born into a prosperous and prestigious family, he chose to live in a small room at VHP office, 20 years he spent their continue to serve as an inspiration for young workers today

Ashok Ji was an institution in himself, his sacrifice, simplicity, and dedication will serve as an inspiration to crores of young people during this birth centenary year

Even while unwell and at an advanced age, inspiration that drove him to work for 16 hours a day came solely from his exemplary patriotism

Ashok Ji held immense reverence for Hindu Dharma, Vedas, Upanishads, Indian culture, and tradition of saints, and remained wholeheartedly dedicated to their cause throughout his life

Ashok Ji used to say that Hindu Dharma should be taken to the world not merely because we are Hindus, but because Hindu Dharma alone is concerned with the welfare of entire world

Ram Janmabhoomi movement was deeply ingrained in his thoughts, he believed that India would attain a position of honour in world only when remnants of the period of foreign rule were removed and a grand Ram Temple was built

There was no distinction between his personal and public life, having imbibed the mantra of living for nation, he merged his personal life with this larger purpose and accepted the work of the organisation as a form of spiritual discipline

When society forgets its heroes, an ideological vacuum emerges, and young people begin to look for their heroes in distant civilizations, that is why life of Ashok Ji and this birth centenary are of immense significance

After Prime Minister Modi Ji came to power, all obstacles were removed within just five years, and a grand Ram Temple was built without any bloodshed

Today, 11 Shri Ram Stambhs were digitally inaugurated, which will continue to carry the message of Shri Ram Van Gaman Path and life of Prabhu Shri Ram to future generations for the next thousand years

27 SEP 2026 7:40PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today addressed the inaugural ceremony of the centenary year celebrations organised in New Delhi to commemorate the birth anniversary of former President of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP), Ashok Singhal. Several dignitaries were present on the occasion.

Addressing the gathering, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that it is a matter of pride for all of us to be present here for the inauguration of the centenary celebrations of the revered Ashok Ji. He said that Ashok Ji was born a hundred years ago and remained exemplary at every stage of his life. As a student, he excelled; as a Swayamsevak, he excelled; and as a Pracharak, he continued to distinguish himself. When he was entrusted with the responsibility of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad, he continued to lead a life devoted to Hindutva with unwavering dedication until his last breath and succeeded in his mission. Such personalities are rarely seen. Shri Shah said that simplicity, exemplary patriotism, devotion to Dharma, commitment to the Swayamsevak ideal and a spirit of struggle—all these qualities were embodied together in Ashok Ji’s life. He was born into a highly prestigious and affluent family. Despite being born into such a family, he remained steadfastly simple in his way of life, the result of which is before us today. He said that we have witnessed the construction of the Ram Janmabhoomi temple, for which the entire Hindu society had been making sacrifices, struggling and coming together for the moment that had been awaited for five and a half centuries. He said that the room at the VHP, where Ashok Ji spent twenty years of his life, has today become almost like an exhibition space for workers. To live with such simplicity and uphold such exemplary patriotism is truly rare.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that even at an advanced age, Ashok Ji would work for sixteen hours a day. His sole source of inspiration was exemplary patriotism. Ashok Ji held immense respect for Hindu Dharma, the Vedas, the Upanishads, Sanskrit, Indian culture and the tradition of saints. Throughout his life, he maintained a deep sense of reverence for all these. He believed that if anyone or anything could contribute to the welfare of the entire universe, it was Hindu Dharma, the Vedas and the Upanishads. Citing the Shanti Mantra as an example, he explained that the objective of enhancing the stature of Hindu Dharma and establishing it in the world was not because we are Hindus, but because Hindu Dharma envisions the welfare of the entire universe. He had said that Guru Golwalkar Ji’s words were that the foundation of our work could only be selfless and pure love, and nothing else. Such an exalted personality remained a Swayamsevak throughout his life. Ashok Ji faithfully followed every discipline of the life of a Pracharak, without seeking glorification or publicity.

Shri Amit Shah said that when it comes to struggle, Ashok Ji is known to everyone for his spirit of struggle. The Ram Janmabhoomi movement was deeply embedded in his heart and mind. He firmly believed that India could attain a position of glory and prestige in the world only by removing the stigma of slavery and constructing a grand Ram Temple. He devoted his entire life to the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. Shri Shah said that when the then Government of Uttar Pradesh ordered a brutal lathi charge, Ashok Ji reached the frontline in disguise. He was also injured in the lathi charge. He said that the image of Ashok Ji wiping blood from his face with a gamchha should remain etched in the memory of the youth for a hundred years. What true dedication means is evident from Ashok Ji’s life and deeds.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that the Vishwa Hindu Parishad, the institution of saints, the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, the construction of the temple and the Sangh were among the subjects closest to Ashok Ji’s heart. He always spoke openly about these causes and worked to advance them. All these institutions and causes became synonymous with his identity. He himself was an institution. Ashok Ji’s life is an institution in itself for many adolescents and young people. He expressed confidence that the celebration of Ashok Ji’s birth centenary would make him a source of inspiration for many young people and adolescents throughout their lives. The essence of his life, his penance, his simplicity and his dedication and endeavour are qualities worthy of emulation by every young person. The remembrance of his life will naturally continue to awaken and inspire the youth.

Shri Amit Shah said that there was no distinction between Ashok Ji’s personal and public life. He had imbibed the ideal of living for the nation and merged his personal life completely with this principle. He accepted organisational work as a form of spiritual practice. He said that merely remembering Ashok Ji’s name is not the purpose of the programme. The centenary year is an endeavour to take his qualities to every household, particularly to the youth. Some people ask why there is a need to celebrate the birth centenary of someone who never sought publicity. I would humbly say that gratitude is not merely a sentiment; it is a national necessity. The birth centenary is necessary so that the entire country and Hindus across the world can express their gratitude to Ashok Ji. When a nation and society do not remember their heroes and fail to take their lives and teachings to the youth, an ideological vacuum emerges. There are no ideals to look up to, no direction to follow and no source of inspiration. People then begin looking for ideals in civilisations thousands of kilometres away. Therefore, it is essential to ensure that an ideological vacuum does not arise in society, that worthy ideals are placed before the people, and that the life of Ashok Ji provides direction and inspiration. This is why celebrating his birth centenary is extremely important.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that today we witnessed presentations of various service initiatives that embody the essence of Hindutva, including prayers at the temples of Sant Ravidas Ji and Maharishi Valmiki Ji, the Ganga Aarti in Prayagraj, Ganga conservation, service to Gaumata, the commemoration of the Ram Setu movement, and the donation of artificial limbs in Ayodhya. The digital inauguration of 11 Shri Ram Stambhs was also held. These pillars commemorate the route taken by Maryada Purushottam Shri Ram during his exile. Without uttering a word, these pillars will convey to generations to come the message of the Ram Van Gaman Path and the virtues of Shri Ram.

Shri Amit Shah said that there is a sense of regret that Ashok Ji, who had dedicated himself to the struggle for the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, could not witness the Bhoomi Pujan or see the temple completed. However, he never worked with the objective of witnessing the fulfilment of his efforts in his own lifetime. He would always say that this was a struggle spanning generations. He said that countless people would fight, several generations would pass, and only then would victory be achieved. He said that wherever Ashok Ji’s soul may be, it must be experiencing that the transformation that came about in the country in 2014 changed the direction of governance. After Prime Minister Modi came to office, the governmental obstacles were removed within just five years, and the grand temple of Prabhu Shri Ram was constructed without bloodshed. He said that this is not only a matter of peace and satisfaction for the country, but also for all devotees of Shri Ram across the world.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that he shares Ashok Ji’s faith that the construction of the Ram Temple would open a new path for India’s progress. He said that our ideas, our culture, our Dharma and its virtues would reach people across the world. He said that Ashok Ji believed that one should remain committed to Hindutva because the welfare of the entire universe is possible only on the basis of the ideals of Hindutva. He expressed the hope that the youth of the country would continue to draw values and inspiration from Ashok Ji’s personality, life, contributions and words for generations to come.

headline: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graces the 15th Graduation Day Ceremony of Sree Uthradom Thirunal (SUT) Academy of Medical Sciences in Thiruvananthapuram
fullText:
Vice President's Secretariat

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graces the 15th Graduation Day Ceremony of Sree Uthradom Thirunal (SUT) Academy of Medical Sciences in Thiruvananthapuram

“Technology Can Assist a Doctor, But Cannot Replace the Human Aspects of a Doctor”: Vice-President urges medical graduates to combine scientific excellence with human compassion

Access to Higher Education is Central to the Vision of Viksit Bharat: Vice-President

27 SEP 2026 6:23PM by PIB Delhi

Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today attended the 15th Graduation Day Ceremony of Sree Uthradom Thirunal (SUT) Academy of Medical Sciences in Thiruvananthapuram, as the Chief Guest.

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the 15th Graduation Day Ceremony of Sree Uthradom Thirunal (SUT) Academy of Medical Sciences, Thiruvananthapuram today.

Governor of Keralam Shri Rajendra Viswanath Arlekar; Minister for Labour, Animal Husbandry and Women and Child… pic.twitter.com/G4prIanwxm

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) September 27, 2026

Addressing the graduating students, the Vice-President highlighted the important place of SUT Academy of Medical Sciences in Keralam’s healthcare and medical education landscape.

“The true strength of a medical institute lies in the quality of education it provides, the doctors it produces, the research it undertakes and the patients it serves,” the Vice-President said.

Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan said the graduating doctors are entering healthcare at an extraordinary time, when Artificial Intelligence, robotics, digital health, advanced imaging and precision medicine are transforming the sector.

In this context, he said, the inauguration of Robotic Surgery and Computer-Aided Diagnosis facilities at the Institute is significant and reflects the importance of keeping medical education and healthcare aligned with technological progress.

However, he stressed that technology must never displace the human dimension of medicine. “Technology can assist a doctor, but it cannot replace the human aspects of a doctor,” he said. “A machine can analyse. A robot can assist. An algorithm can identify patterns. But a patient still needs a doctor who can listen, understand, reassure and take responsibility,” he added.

The Vice-President urged the graduates to protect the trust represented by the white coat by being accurate in diagnosis, honest in communication, compassionate in treatment and ethical in every decision.He emphasised that scientific excellence and human compassion must always go together.

The Vice-President said Bharat is striding confidently towards the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047 articulated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi.He said the Prime Minister has emphasised that Viksit Bharat can be achieved only when every State, district and village develops, and noted that access to higher education is at the core of this national vision.

Highlighting the expansion of medical education over the past twelve years, Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan said that while there was only one AIIMS in New Delhi earlier, 12 new AIIMS have been established.

The Vice-President said he has attended convocations across the length and breadth of Bharat and observed a welcome trend of more women receiving degrees and medals than men.

He noted that at the present graduation ceremony, 60 women and 32 men are receiving undergraduate degrees, while 5 women and 2 men doctors are receiving postgraduate degrees.He described this as a welcome development.

Giving three guiding principles to the graduating doctors, the Vice-President urged them to carry:Knowledge in their minds, Compassion in their hearts, Integrity in their conduct.

He asked the graduates to be confident while remaining humble, ambitious while remaining ethical, technologically advanced while remaining compassionate, and successful while remaining connected to society.He also urged the young doctors to “always say No to drugs.”

Concluding his address, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan wished the graduates a successful, meaningful and fulfilling professional journey and said, “May you always remember that the greatest privilege of being a doctor is the opportunity to make a difference in another human being’s life.”He also wished SUT Academy of Medical Sciences continued growth as a centre of excellence in medical education, healthcare, research and innovation.

The ceremony was attended by Governor of Tamil Nadu and Keralam Shri Rajendra Viswanath Arlekar; Minister for Labour, Animal Husbandry and Women and Child Development, Government of Keralam, Smt. Bindhu Krishna; Chairman, SUT Academy of Medical Sciences, Dr. A. C. Shanmugam; Vice Chancellor, Kerala University of Health Sciences, Dr. Mohanan Kunnummal; faculty, staff, graduating students and their families.

fullText:

INDIAN NAVAL SHIPS SAHYADRI AND KULISH CONCLUDE PARTICIPATION IN ADMM-PLUS MARITIME SECURITY JOINT COOPERATION ACTIVITY

27 SEP 2026 5:52PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Navy’s frontline stealth frigate, INS Sahyadri, and missile corvette, INS Kulish, concluded their participation in the 23rd ADMM-Plus Experts’ Working Group on Maritime Security Joint Cooperation Activity (EWG-MS JCA) at Subic Bay, Philippines, with the Closing Ceremony held on 25 Sep 2026.

The activity commenced on 21 Sep 2026 with the Opening Ceremony at Naval Operating Base Subic, hosted by the Philippine Navy and co-chaired by Japan. The Harbour Phase featured Subject Matter Expert Exchanges on Peace and Security, ASEAN Navy Chiefs’ Meeting and Guidelines for Maritime Interaction (ANCM-GMI), Senior Enlisted Leadership and Marine Environmental Protection, alongside sporting events and an International Day and Cultural Show.

On 22 Sep 2026, Indian Naval personnel participated in Operational Synchronisation and a Tabletop Exercise, followed by a Pre-Sail Conference to coordinate the Sea Phase. A community engagement programme was also conducted at the Shepherds of the Hill Center, Zambales.

The Sea Phase comprised coordinated serials including Search and Rescue, Hydrographic Survey, Casualty and Medical Evacuation, Deck Landing Qualification and assistance to vessels aground. These activities provided valuable opportunities to enhance operational coordination and interoperability at sea.

The successful conduct of the EWG-MS JCA highlighted the value of professional interaction and practical multilateral engagement in strengthening maritime cooperation. India’s participation reaffirmed its commitment to regional partnerships in consonance with the Act East Policy and the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions).
